candidate.answerReason: The independent heads events have intersection probability (1/2)(1/2)=1/4.

methods.label: Multiply independent probabilities
methods.explanation:
Because the tosses are independent, multiply their heads probabilities:
\[
P(\text{heads on both tosses})=\frac12\cdot\frac12=\frac14.
\]
methods.levelReason: Uses independent repetition and elementary fraction multiplication, both within the required-course scope.

methods.label: List the ordered outcomes
methods.explanation:
Let \(H\) denote heads and \(T\) denote tails. Since the tosses are independent and each has equally likely heads and tails, the four ordered outcomes
\[
HH,\quad HT,\quad TH,\quad TT
\]
are equally likely. The letters record the first and second toss in order, so the list includes every possibility exactly once. Only \(HH\) has two heads, giving probability \(\frac14\).
methods.levelReason: Uses elementary enumeration and favorable outcomes divided by total outcomes. Independence justifies equal likelihood without a conditional-probability formula.
